question.text: Scenario: Meera Srinivasan is the compliance officer at Galaxy Research Services, a SEBI-registered research entity. She discovers the following situations during her quarterly review: (1) Analyst Rajan published a Buy report on PharmaTech Ltd and his wife purchased PharmaTech shares 15 days before the report was published. (2) The firm received Rs.50 lakh from InfoSys Corp for investment banking advisory services 6 months ago. Analyst Priya, who covers InfoSys Corp, did not disclose this in her latest research report. (3) Analyst Vikram's compensation for the year was partly determined based on the revenue his research helped generate from brokerage services for specific clients. (4) The research team is located on the same floor as the investment banking team, sharing common meeting rooms and a common server for document storage. (5) Analyst Deepa received a call from the CEO of MicroChip Ltd sharing that the company will announce a major acquisition next week. This information has not been made public. Question 1 of 5: Galaxy Research Services has, in its compliance policy, formally designated each research analyst's immediate-family spouse as an "associate" of the analyst for the purpose of Regulation 16. On that basis, how should Meera classify Rajan's wife purchasing PharmaTech shares 15 days before his Buy report?

answer.text: This is perfectly acceptable as the restriction is only 5 days
This violates Regulation 16(2) — associates of RAs cannot trade within 30 days before publication of a research report
This is acceptable because the firm's policy does not list spouses as associates
The 30-day restriction applies only to Sell recommendations

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 16(2) prohibits RAs and their "associates" from dealing in the recommended security within 30 days before and 5 days after publication of the research report (NISM-Series-XV workbook p. 276). Because Galaxy's compliance policy expressly designates the analyst's spouse as an associate (as stated in the stem), the wife's purchase 15 days before publication squarely violates the 30-day pre-publication restriction. The Trap: Option A applies the wrong window (5 days is the post-publication tail, not the pre-publication restriction). Option D fabricates a Buy/Sell distinction that the regulation does not draw. Option C is the defensible reading under the original stem because the workbook pages checked (pp. 261, 263, 276, 279) do not explicitly state that a wife/spouse is automatically an "associate" for Regulation 16 purposes — the audit flagged this as the source of ambiguity. Note: The original stem assumed without stating that Rajan's wife was his "associate". The stem now imports that classification from the firm's compliance policy, making option B uniquely correct once the spouse-as-associate definition is fixed (NISM-Series-XV workbook p. 276 for the 30-day window).
